sections.heading: C — General Driving
sections.markdown:
## C — General Driving

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A61
Before a turn, check controls, pedestrians and vehicles, signal, and enter the nearest lane in the intended direction. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A61
Look through the turn as far as possible, accelerate smoothly and ensure the signal cancels afterward. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A61
Start a right turn from the rightmost part of your lane without swinging left first. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A61
Start a left turn from the leftmost part of your lane and yield to oncoming traffic. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A61
When multiple lanes permit the same turn, keep the corresponding lane through the turn until it is finished. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A61
An intersection is any meeting of traffic paths, including side streets, freeway entries and driveways or shopping-center entrances. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A62
Look in both directions even when crossing a one-way street because a vehicle may be traveling the wrong way. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A62
At intersections, slow and search for controls, traffic, pedestrians, cyclists, road conditions and blocked sight lines. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A62
Check cross traffic even when it faces red or a stop sign, and be ready to yield to prevent a crash. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A62
After stopping, check traffic and cyclists with a left-right-left search before entry. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A62
Before moving on green, confirm the path is clear and cross traffic has stopped. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A62
Do not enter a lane merely because an approaching driver signals a turn; the signal may be mistaken or refer to a later turn. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A62
If a fixed obstruction blocks a cross-street view, edge forward slowly only far enough to see and wait for traffic to clear before turning. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A62
If cars in one lane hide another lane, wait for them to pass rather than pushing the vehicle’s nose into the hidden lane. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A62
Vehicles entering a circle or roundabout yield to circulating traffic unless police or a traffic-control device directs otherwise. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A62
Enter a roundabout to the right of the center island and travel counterclockwise. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A62
At the described small-island roundabout, raised inner pavement accommodates trucks while ordinary vehicles remain in the outer travel lane. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A63
Exit a traffic circle with a right turn and pay close attention to signs and lane markings. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A63
In the described rotary, a driver exiting within 2 exits is advised to use the rightmost lane unless signs or markings assign another lane. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A63
Slow on entering a circle, yield to circulating traffic, follow lane lines and signal the exit. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A63
A lane change requires mirror checks and a head turn toward the intended side to inspect the blind spot. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A63
Blind spots include areas hidden by vehicle structure and areas the mirrors do not cover. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A63
For a lane change, find a gap, signal, look again, adjust speed, move over and cancel the signal afterward. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A64
Lane-change precautions also apply to freeway entry and moving onto a road from its curb or shoulder. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A64
Before moving sideways, check mirrors for passing traffic and look over the relevant shoulder for vehicles near the rear corner. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A64
Watch particularly for motorcycles and bicycles during a lane-change check. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A64
Make rearward checks brief so your eyes return promptly to the road ahead. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A64
Inspect every relevant lane because another driver may be moving toward the same gap. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A64
Signal your intended movement at least 100 feet before making the change. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A64
Use the expressway acceleration lane to approach traffic speed before merging, while looking for a suitable gap. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A64
For the described expressway entry, signal left, check the rearview mirror and over the shoulder, merge into a clear gap and cancel the signal. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A64
Where an expressway entrance lacks an acceleration lane, stop before entry, wait for a traffic gap, then accelerate and merge. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A65
Traffic already on an expressway need not yield to entering traffic, so avoid merging at a speed that obstructs its flow. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A65
The expressway guidance says to remain in the right lane unless passing and not to pass on the right or shoulder. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A65
Before expressway passing, signal, check mirrors and look over the shoulder to confirm clearance. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A65
Do not increase speed while another vehicle is passing you. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A65
Pass promptly and safely, avoid lingering alongside, and return right only after the entire passed vehicle appears in the rearview mirror. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A65
Avoid cruising in the neighboring driver’s blind spot. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A65
For an expressway exit, move right early and signal; begin slowing in the deceleration lane rather than the through lane. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A65
Slow to the ramp’s posted speed and ensure the exit signal cancels. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A65
Stop on an expressway only for an emergency; signal and pull as far off the pavement as the shoulder allows. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F42 | anchor: A65
Raise the hood to request help after the described emergency stop. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F43 | anchor: A65
Never reverse, walk or stand on an expressway’s traveled portion. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-F44 | anchor: A66
Long straight highway travel can cause drowsiness or reduced awareness, so continued concentration is essential. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F45 | anchor: A66
The manual’s alertness tips include a cool cabin, scanning ahead, conversation or music and small speed variations. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F46 | anchor: A66
At the first drowsiness warning, use the nearest rest or service area to stretch, nap or change drivers if possible. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F47 | anchor: A66
Do not depend on stay-awake drugs to make tired driving safe. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F48 | anchor: A66
Passing on a two-lane road uses the opposing lane, so signal and start only when it is clear. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F49 | anchor: A66
The manual gives 10 to 12 seconds as a passing-time guide at 50 to 55 miles per hour. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F50 | anchor: A66
Assess passing space before an approaching vehicle, hill, curve, intersection or road obstruction. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F51 | anchor: A66
Before passing, check oncoming traffic, mirrors and the shoulder blind spot, signal and enter the left passing lane. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F52 | anchor: A66
After passing, wait until the whole vehicle is visible in the rearview mirror, signal and shoulder-check before returning right. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F53 | anchor: A66
After returning to the right lane, adjust speed and cancel the passing signal. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-F54 | anchor: A67
When being passed, remain in your lane and keep a steady speed. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-F55 | anchor: A67
If an overtaker abandons the pass and drops behind, you may need to increase speed before an oncoming vehicle arrives. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-F56 | anchor: A67
The highway-passing illustration allows over 1,600 feet, roughly one-third mile, for the combined opposing vehicles’ travel. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-F57 | anchor: A67
A distant oncoming vehicle can appear nearly stationary while already being too close for a pass. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-F58 | anchor: A67
Do not start passing within one-third mile of a hill or curve that blocks the view ahead. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-F59 | anchor: A67
Avoid passing at intersections, crossroads or shopping-center entries where traffic or people may enter the road. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-F60 | anchor: A67
Do not pass while approaching a railroad crossing or bridge. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

Misconceptions: mirrors alone do not cover every lane-change blind spot. [A63]
Mnemonic: observe, signal, find space, recheck, complete.
Glossary: a blind spot is an area that vehicle structure or mirrors prevent you from seeing. [A63]
Dynamic facts: municipal restrictions and current penalty amounts retain their local and dated scope.

items.why: Control exceptions and clear-path checks need scenario practice.
Direct observation, gap decisions and road-specific exceptions differ.
Road division, warning devices and release conditions are load-bearing.
Sequential maneuvers and conditional reference points need procedural practice.

corpus_stability.reason: Working assessment for the pinned Rev 4/24 snapshot: the frontmatter supplies one revision marker and this intake provides no evidence of more than annual revision. This is an inference for the fixed corpus, not a measured publication cadence; legal and administrative changes still require monitoring.
